note: Oakley Networks (data-leak prevention, Salt Lake City per the firm's 2008 listing) was bought by Raytheon in 2007, the acquirer the firm's own page names. The firm's since-year is 2004; no record on disk names the round it entered, so the stage is undetermined.

Wikipedia: in 2007 Ocarina secured a $12M Series A from Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and Highland Capital, the firm's 2007 since-year; the 2009 Form D is the $20M follow-on, not the entry. Dell bought Ocarina in 2010 (the firm's page names Dell).
Oculeve (dry-eye device) was acquired by Allergan in 2015, the acquirer the firm's page names; South San Francisco as in the NEA book.

Offermatic (card-linked offers, 2010-11 Form D filings at 440 N. Wolfe Road, Sunnyvale). The firm listed it as Private 2012-14 and then dropped it; no exit or shutdown is on record, so the state is unknown. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Okay (okayhq.com, engineering analytics, San Francisco) was bought by Stripe in May 2023 (TechCrunch: it raised $6.6M in total from Sequoia and Kleiner Perkins after YC W20). The Wikidata country CZ and acquirer 'OKAY Holding' belong to a Czech namesake: country US. The round the firm entered in 2021 is not named on record.

funding_rounds.round: total raised before the sale (YC W20, then Sequoia and Kleiner Perkins)

note: One Kings Lane (home decor flash sales, San Francisco) was acquired by Bed Bath & Beyond in 2016; aligned with Greylock, IVP and Tiger Global.
ONI Systems (optical networking, San Jose) went public in 2000 and was acquired by Ciena in 2002; Kleiner Perkins funds filed 13Gs on it in 2001-02. No record gives the round the firm entered.

Wikipedia: Sequoia led the $75M Series A (Feb 2025) and GV and Kleiner Perkins led the $210M round of July 2025, the firm's entry (its own post is dated 2025-07-15), a round after the A, so Growth. Headquartered in Miami (Wikipedia), as GV and Coatue carry it.

Ophthonix (iZon vision-correction lenses, 1491 Poinsettia Avenue, Vista per its 2010 Form D). No exit or shutdown is on record, so the state is unknown. The Form D seed band is doubtful: the company predates the 2008 Form D coverage and Joe Lacob sat on its board for years before 2010. The base also carries it as izon-formerly-ophthonix and opthonix. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Opstrace (open-source observability, 35 Divisadero Street, San Francisco per its 2020 Form D) was acquired by GitLab in December 2021, the acquirer the firm's page names. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

OptiMedica (cataract laser systems, Santa Clara per the firm's 2008 listing) was acquired by Abbott in 2013. The firm's since-year (2005) predates the 2009 Form D the band reads, so the entry date is likely earlier than the band's.
Optimizely was acquired by Episerver in 2020 (the firm's page names Episerver); aligned with every sibling book.

Wikipedia: KPCB led Optoro's $50M Series C in December 2014 from its Green Growth Fund, the firm's entry (the band's 2014-11-25 is the same round's Form D). Returns-logistics software, Washington DC, still private; no priced round at $1B on record.

The 2006 S-1's related-party table shows KPCB Holdings (for KPCB X-A and X-B) buying 3,389,831 Series A shares in the January 2004 $11.0M round, when Joe Lacob joined the board. La Jolla (San Diego). Bankrupt in 2018 and sold to Nalpropion, so acquired with a successor.

Wikipedia: on 2011-01-05 OSIsoft announced a $135M minority investment by TCV and KPCB (the Green Growth Fund on the firm's archived page), an at-scale entry into a 1980 company, so Growth, not the Form D seed band. AVEVA bought OSIsoft in 2021.

The firm's since-year is 2004, when Brook Byers joined the board and KP entrepreneur-in-residence Hugh Martin became CEO; the 2010 S-1 shows KPCB Holdings in the Series E and F but covers only rounds from 2007, so the 2004 round is not named. The 2013 Form D date is a later round.

basis: Sale consideration (Erik 2026-09-22; decisions.md R5): the firm's 'Palm' card (since 1998, founder Jeff Hawkins) is its Handspring investment; KPCB held about 10% of Handspring when Palm bought it in 2003 (S-4) and KPCB VIII then held palmOne stock (2004 proxy). Palm itself was a 3Com unit in 1998. Handspring is its own row.

note: Wikipedia: in February 2011 Path raised its second round, $8.5M from KPCB (iFund/sFund on the archived page) and Index, after the 2010 seed, which reads Series A; the Form D of 2011-01-28 is this round. Acquired by Daum Kakao in 2015 (the app shut in 2018).

funding_rounds.lead: Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers; Index Ventures

note: The firm's Pattern is Pattern Brands (patternbrands.com, home-goods brand group of Emmett Shine, New York). The prefilled public status and $550M float come from a weak CIK join to Pattern Group, an unrelated listed company; Pattern Brands is private with no exit found (web check 2026-09-30). First Round's Pattern (a defunct SF SaaS row) looks like another company. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

The firm's since-year is 2017, when Peloton (founded 2012) had already raised four rounds; its 2017 financing was the $325M Series E led by TCV, and KPCB Holdings signs the pre-IPO investor rights agreement (S-1 exhibit). Any 2017 entry is Growth; KP's own round is not cited.

The firm's post of 2024-02-21 announces it led PermitFlow's Series A (YC W22, New York), matching the 2024 since-year; its 2024-12-03 post covers the Series B. Construction-permitting software; no priced round at $1B on record.

Persona (identity verification, San Francisco; SiliconANGLE). The prefilled status acquired and country RU are Wikidata joins to namesakes. The firm's since-year is 2021, after the January 2020 Series A, so its entry is the 2021 Series B or C (Growth); which one is not on record. Mark: the $200M Series D at $2B (2025-04-30), as Coatue, Insight and Ribbit carry it.

Phantom Cyber (security orchestration, phantom.us, Palo Alto) was bought by Splunk in 2018 for about $350M. The firm's since-year 2016 matches the $13.5M Series A KPCB led that year (model, not cited). The a16z, Lightspeed and Sequoia 'Phantom' rows are the crypto wallet, a different company.

Pharmacopeia (combinatorial chemistry, Princeton NJ as in Greylock and IVP) was acquired by Ligand in 2008; Kleiner Perkins funds filed 13Gs on it in 1997-98. No record names the round the firm entered.
Pharmacyclics (Sunnyvale) was founded in 1991, the firm's since-year, and bought by AbbVie in 2015. No record names the founding round the firm entered.

The firm's post (2025-09-18) says it led Phia's seed round; the firm dates the investment 2024, as does the Form D first sale (2024-04-30), so Seed, not the band's Series A. Graduated: the company's release of 2026-01-27 (New York) announces a $35M Series A led by Notable Capital with returning investor Kleiner Perkins, at $185M. Momentum check 2026-09-30: that Series A at $185M is the last priced round, below $1B.

Photon Dynamics (flat-panel test equipment, San Jose; KP general partner Floyd Kvamme its chairman) was acquired by Orbotech in 2008; Kleiner Perkins funds filed 13Gs in 1998-99. The entry round is not on record.

Pilot (pilot.com, startup bookkeeping and tax, San Francisco). Last priced mark: the Series C extended to $100M with Whale Rock and Bezos Expeditions at $1.2B (PYMNTS, 2021-03-26), over 24 months old. Sequoia's row cites a vendor page for the same figure. Union Square Ventures' Pilot is Pilot Fiber, a different company.

The firm's since-year is 2015, when Pinterest (founded 2010) raised its $367M Series G at $11B, a late round in any case, so Growth; KP's own round is not cited. Market cap $10.7B on 2026-09-30 (StockAnalysis), fresher than the prefilled $18.7B and within 7% of the $10B edge.

The firm's Pivotal is Pivotal Corporation, the CRM software maker whose 2001 10-K gives its head office at 224 West Esplanade, North Vancouver, BC and lists KPCB VI at 3.61%; chinadotcom (CDC) bought it in February 2004. The Wikidata ES country and the former-unicorn line (Pivotal Software, 2013) are other companies; the site's current blurb conflates them. Entry round not on record.

Pixtronix (MEMS displays, Andover MA per the firm's listing) was acquired by Qualcomm in 2012. The firm's since-year is 2005; the 2009 Form D filings are later rounds, and no record names the round of 2005.

TechCrunch 2018-12-11: the $250M Series C at $2.65B was led by Mary Meeker with capital from Kleiner Perkins' growth fund (a Digital Growth Fund position, IN under D2). Mark aligned with the sibling books: the $13.4B 2021 unicorn-list figure yields to the $8B employee share sale (TechCrunch, 2026-02-26), so the band moves from 10b_plus to 1b_plus.

The firm's post of 2021-11-16 announces 'our partnership with PlanetScale' and its lead investment in the $50M Series C, its entry (since-year 2021). Momentum check 2026-09-30: the company's blog (latest post 2026-09-10) and the firm's posts show no later priced round, none at $1B.
Plex (media server and free ad-supported streaming) is based in Campbell, California (Wikipedia). The firm's since-year is 2014; no record names the round, and no priced round at $1B is known.
Power Integrations (power-conversion chips, San Jose). KP general partner Floyd Kvamme has sat on the board since September 1989 (2001 10-K), which dates the relationship but names no round.
Wikipedia: KPCB led the $70M Series D in September 2013 (a Digital Growth Fund position on the archived page). Allscripts bought Practice Fusion in 2018.

The firm's post (2018-05-15): Kleiner Perkins led a $4.5M seed in Prisma. Graduated: the company's blog announces a $12M Series A led by Amplify Partners (2020-06-26). Tech.eu calls it a German-American startup with offices in Berlin and San Francisco; Berlin, DE. The Wikidata CH country and acquired status are namesakes; Prisma is private.

Productboard (founded in Prague, headquartered in San Francisco; Wikipedia names offices in both), aligned with Tiger Global's San Francisco. The firm's since-year is 2018, before the Index-led Series A and Sequoia-led Series B reported in the sibling notes; the round KP entered is not on record.

The firm's post: 'When we first invested in Progyny in May 2010' (then Auxogyn, incorporated 2008 as Auxogen Bioscience); the round word is not given. New York (Wikipedia). The base also carries it as auxogyn-inc.
Propel (Providers app for SNAP/EBT households, Brooklyn, so New York). The firm's since-year is 2018; the round is not on record, and no priced round at $1B is known.
Proterra (electric buses and batteries, Burlingame) filed Chapter 11 in August 2023 and sold its businesses (batteries to Volvo, transit buses to Phoenix Motor), so acquired with successors.
Pulmonx is headquartered in Redwood City, as the firm's 2010 listing also gives.

Q (q.ai, founded 2022 by Aviad Maizels, headquartered in Ramat Gan) raised $24.5M in January 2023 from Kleiner Perkins, GV and others (Calcalist), matching the firm's 2023 since-year; the round is not named. Apple bought it in January 2026 for about $1.5-2B. The Wikidata NO country is a namesake.

QuantumScape was founded in 2010 (Wikipedia); the firm's since-year is 2010 and John Doerr has sat on the board since December 2010 (2020 S-1). Lightspeed's own card calls its 2010 entry the Series A; KP's participation in that round is inferred, not cited.

Wikipedia: KPCB co-led the $68M Series C in September 2012 (Digital Growth Fund). Quirky filed Chapter 11 on 2015-09-22 and its assets, site and products were bought by Q Holdings for $4.7M, which relaunched it: acquired with a successor under the asset-sale rule; the a16z row reads defunct.
